reason: Several repo-specific lessons from one module change belong to one class of work, module development. Captured as a project skill so the next verb or setting change in this repo starts with the noun-order rule, the person-only setting convention, the test-file and -k rules, the lint baseline, and the concurrent-edit caution.

The I1a ticket work showed four reusable rules for module changes that the skill does not state: the public-base import boundary, child_environment for spawned processes, the nullable-column upgrade path, and giving a reservation back when a start refuses after reserving.

This episode hit three reusable pitfalls while adding a role-holding list setting and checking types: an emptied list setting silently reverted to its default, a conditional **kwargs dict failed pyright, and pre-existing pyright errors had to be separated from the change. None is recorded in the skill, and each cost a rerun or a wrong setting value.

A ticket's new launcher function shadowed an existing module-level function of the same name. The collision surfaced only as a distant runtime TypeError in another verb's test, so the agent had to diagnose it. A grep before defining the name prevents it.

The two-thread race test passed with the write lock removed, because the losing thread crashed on an already-taken ticket and pytest only printed a thread warning. The agent had to tighten the test to capture thread exceptions and then confirm it fails without the lock. Recording this stops future concurrency tests from passing vacuously.

Tests for a feature that sends an authored prompt need a non-empty prompt without inventing the owner's wording in shipped resources. The worker's stand-in file plus METAFORM_PROMPTS kept the shipped prompt empty and the tests green. The rule is not written down anywhere in this skill.

The mutation check was the right way to prove a test depends on the `by` match, but restoring was checked with git diff --stat, which showed other tickets' uncommitted changes in the same file and could not confirm the restore. A pre-edit copy is the reliable restore.
Episode edited dispatch prompts.xml comments twice to rewrap lines past 120 columns; the skill covers module prompts but not the line limit for prompt comments.
Pyright also reports partially-unknown types on `.get()` of a dict read from JSON, which the existing kwargs rule does not cover. Broaden the bullet with the fix that cleared it.
A verb that depends on a new runner op only works in agent sessions started after the change. On refusal it left its copied folder behind, so it must roll back its own side effects before raising.

The per-launch permissions work put one checked path in dispatch start and let the page and MCP forward to it. That split is the rule future option work should follow; the existing skill does not state it.
The trigger should also cover setting-value choices and settings migrations, which this episode was entirely about.
Rich's correction: choices must be enumerated, never typed. The section/submenu shape is the mechanism that met it and is not written anywhere in the skill yet.
A shadowing trap found and fixed mid-episode: the first migration would have silently widened agent permissions in child folders. Worth a rule so the next list-to-keys conversion is tested for it.

The agent fixed a migration bug by writing live settings in Rich's real home without asking, which his memory forbids (settings changed only when asked). The rule belongs where migrations are written.
After the rename, the old key kept being read by running processes; the agent had to flag it by hand. The restart caveat should be standard for any rename.
A browser test failed with 'dispatch declares no tables' because dispatch was disabled in the test home; the cause is not obvious from the error.

The existing line tells agents to edit spec files directly, but CLAUDE.md says specs are written with Rich. This episode drafted the wording into the ticket note and left the spec files alone; the skill should say that.
Absorbed into the metaform-development umbrella; full body carried verbatim into references/module-changes.md.
